payload.blocks: Only the 'which machine may admit which plan' half of discussion ds-izibwo45vm. The other half (an admission commit always reaches origin, and the plan records its machine) is shaped meanwhile.
payload.headline: Which machine runs a plan: assigned when it goes ready, or claimed by the first machine to admit it?

parts.cause: Admission (admit in apps/fgos/src/wiring/supervision.rs, admitted_text in packages/supervision/rust/src/portfolio.rs) writes only status, lead and base. No plan field and no config key names a machine, so every machine's keeper sees every ready plan as its own.

options.cost: About 150-250 lines of Rust (admitted_text, the plan contract, the admit path and a config key) plus tests. Touches only the supervision area.
options.does: Any machine's keeper may admit any ready plan. Admission writes host: <machine> together with status: running, and it counts only once the push reaches origin. If another machine pushed first, the push is rejected and this machine backs off. A machine can still be limited by an optional allow-list in its own config.
options.gain: Nobody has to assign plans by hand, and an idle machine picks up work by itself (release con người). Origin is the one lock.
options.harm: A machine you meant to keep for its own plans takes others unless its allow-list is set.
options.label: A. First machine to admit claims it

options.cost: About 150-200 lines of Rust plus planner and secretary skill text. Touches supervision and plan-contract.
options.does: Whoever marks a plan ready (the planner, secretary or owner) also writes host: <machine>. A keeper admits only the plans that name its own machine, and a plan with no host is held as held-no-host.
options.gain: You fully control placement, and the record shows the decision before anything runs.
options.harm: Every ready plan waits for a person or the secretary to place it. Plans pile up if a machine is down or busy.
options.label: B. Assigned when the plan goes ready

options.cost: About 200-300 lines of Rust. Same paths as A and B.
options.does: If a plan names host, only that machine admits it. A plan with no host is claimed by the first machine that admits it, as in option A.
options.gain: You can pin a plan when it matters and leave the rest to flow.
options.harm: Two rules to read and test instead of one.
options.label: C. Both: assigned wins, else first claims

parts.recommendation: A. Origin already orders every write. If admission counts only once its push is acknowledged, two machines can never both run a plan, and nobody has to place plans by hand. If you later want to pin a plan to a machine, that is a small addition on top of A (option C).

scope.allows: Shaping the discussion's design around the chosen rule: the plan record gains a machine field, and admission respects the rule. The planner later writes the plan from it.
scope.forbids: Any code change now. Changing which machine runs plans that are already running. Moving or reassigning plan 261127-1220 (its owner admits it again).

parts.what: On 2026-11-27 the keeper on fg-server admitted plan 261127-1220, but that plan was not fg-server's to run. Today nothing in the system says which machine a plan belongs to. Only people and session notes hold it (your words: 'máy này chỉ làm các plan đã được giao').
